## Accessibility statement for the NHSBSA Producing Quality Analysis Playbook

This statement applies to the Producing Quality Analysis Playbook. It does not cover the other
NHSBSA sites and playbooks linked from it, which publish their own statements.

We want as many people as possible to be able to use this playbook. It is built to meet the Web
Content Accessibility Guidelines version 2.2 at level AA, and meets several level AAA criteria as
well.

## What we have done

The site is built from plain text with Quarto, so its content is headings, paragraphs, lists,
tables and links rather than images of any of those things.

- Every section is in the sidebar, on every page, in the same order, and a skip link takes you past
  it to the content
- The page title, the heading and the navigation label all name the same thing, so the page you
  arrive at is the page you expected
- Help and the glossary sit in the same place in the footer of every page
- Links say where they go rather than reading "click here" or "read more"
- Text reflows to a single column at 320 pixels wide without horizontal scrolling
- Keyboard focus is shown with a visible outline and is never hidden behind the header
- Navigation targets are large enough to hit, and text and interface colours meet the required
  contrast ratios

## What we have checked, and how

Some of the claims above are checked automatically against the built pages every time the site is
rebuilt, rather than being asserted once: that no page scrolls sideways at any of six widths from
320 pixels, that every diagram carries a text alternative and a full description, that every page
has its own browser title, and that a table wide enough to scroll can be reached and scrolled from
the keyboard.

Two of the checks work from a photograph of the screen rather than from the page's code, because
a style that changes on focus is not the same thing as a change a person can see. Every kind of
control on the site is given the keyboard focus and the screen is photographed on either side of
it, and every control that carries a spoken name is compared against the words printed on it.

## Where we go beyond level AA

Five level AAA criteria are met and checked the same way.

| Criterion | What it asks | What the site does |
|---|---|---|
| 1.4.6 Contrast (Enhanced) | 7:1 for body text, 4.5:1 for large text, against the 4.5:1 that AA asks | Links are NHS Dark Blue at 10.93:1, quiet text is NHS Dark Grey at 7.75:1, and the title banner is dark enough that white text on it clears 7:1 at any size |
| 1.4.8 Visual Presentation | No line of prose longer than 80 characters, no justified text, generous line and paragraph spacing | Prose is capped at 80 characters, set ragged right, at 1.6 line spacing |
| 2.5.5 Target Size (Enhanced) | Anything you click or tap is at least 44 by 44 pixels | Navigation, footer and table links are 44 pixels tall. A link inside a sentence takes the criterion's own exception for inline targets, and is also in the sidebar at full size |
| 2.4.9 Link Purpose (Link Only) | Every link makes sense read on its own, out of the sentence around it | No link on the site reads "click here", "read more" or similar, and none uses a bare web address as its text. Every link on the site is checked on every build |
| 2.4.10 Section Headings | Content is organised under headings rather than running on | Every page of any length carries headings, so the on-this-page list is a usable route through it |

## Where we do not meet level AAA

We do not claim level AAA for the site. The W3C advises against requiring AAA as a general policy
for a whole site, because some content cannot satisfy every AAA criterion. What is useful instead
is to say which ones are met, and which are not.

Two are out of reach for guidance of this kind, and saying so is more useful than claiming
otherwise.

**3.1.5 Reading Level** asks that text is understandable by someone with lower secondary school
education, or that a simpler version is provided. This playbook cites clause numbers from GovS 010
and the AQuA Book and uses the vocabulary of analytical assurance, because its readers need the
exact terms to apply the standards. The glossary in the appendices is the partial answer, not a
full one.

**1.4.9 Images of Text** allows images of text only where the presentation is essential. The
diagrams contain a good deal of text in boxes. The layout carries meaning that a list cannot, which
is the argument for them, but it is an argument rather than a certainty. Each one is written out in
full beneath it, so nothing in a diagram is available only as a picture.

## What we have not tested

No screen reader, magnifier or speech input testing has been carried out against the published
site. Automated checks find only the faults they are written to look for, so parts of this site may
still not be fully accessible, and this statement describes the work done rather than a tested
result. If you find a problem, we want to hear about it.

## Reporting a problem

If you find a problem that is not listed here, or you need content in a different format, write to
[analyticalassurance@nhsbsa.nhs.uk](mailto:analyticalassurance@nhsbsa.nhs.uk). Tell us the page,
what you were trying to do, and what happened.

## Enforcement procedure

The Equality and Human Rights Commission is responsible for enforcing the Public Sector Bodies
(Websites and Mobile Applications) (No. 2) Accessibility Regulations 2018. If you are not happy with
how we respond to your complaint, contact the
[Equality Advisory and Support Service](https://www.equalityadvisoryservice.com/).
